highlights.title: GPT-6 Astra Is Here—and OpenAI Thinks It May Kick Off the AGI Era
highlights.summary: OpenAI leaders think the company’s next generation model, which excels at computer use and coding, may mark a major milestone in AI development.
body: OpenAI announced Thursday the launch of its next generation AI model, GPT-6 Astra, which the company claims is state of the art at navigating computers and web browsers, writing software, and solving difficult math problems.

In a press briefing with reporters, OpenAI executives made it clear that they feel very confident about the company’s latest AI model. President and cofounder Greg Brockman says he personally believes the world is now in the era of artificial general intelligence, or AI systems that are generally smarter than humans.

“It’s not unreasonable to feel that we are now in the AGI era,” Brockman told reporters. “I think that if we fast-forward a couple of years, when we look back and say, ‘When was it really that AGI was created?’ I think it's going to be about this time, and I think it might be about this model."

highlights.title: The Most Divisive Civilization Game is Completely Free to Play on Steam for One Week
highlights.summary: Ever wanted to rule your own country, conquer the world by force, or turn your civilization into the planet's ultimate cultural powerhouse, but didn't want to spend $70 for the experience?
body: Civilization 7 is free to play on Steam right now as part of a special Free Play Week celebrating the franchise's 35th anniversary. The promotion runs from Sept. 3 at 10 a.m. PT through Sept. 10 at 10 a.m. PT, giving curious strategists a full week to find out whether the latest take on the classic 4X formula deserves a permanent spot in their libraries. If you decide you want to play more, the game is 50% off to purchase right now for just $34.99.

The game has received several major updates since Civilization 7 's 2025 release, including May's massive Test of Time update, which substantially reworked some of the systems that players were unhappy with at launch. Among the biggest changes was the way civilizations progress through the game's three Ages. Players can now stick with their original civilization throughout an entire campaign rather than being forced to switch civilizations at each Age transition, while new systems such as Syncretism and Affirmation give players more control over how their civilization develops.

highlights.title: OpenAI Cut Off a Billion-Dollar Customer to Avoid Elon Musk
highlights.summary: OpenAI recently estimated its Cursor partnership would make more than $1 billion in revenue a year, WIRED has learned. It still walked away after Elon Musk’s SpaceX acquired the AI coding startup.
body: In a late-night blog post last Friday, OpenAI said it would wind down its partnership with Cursor, the startup behind one of the most popular AI coding tools on the market. The reason OpenAI gave for the decision is effectively that it can’t trust Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX recently acquired Cursor in a $60 billion deal.

In doing so, OpenAI walked away from one of its most important customers. Cursor has long paid OpenAI fees to offer the ChatGPT-maker’s models to developers using its AI coding editor. At the start of 2026, Cursor was one of OpenAI’s top five customers in terms of revenue, people familiar with the matter tell WIRED. By the spring of this year, OpenAI estimated Cursor would bring in more than $1 billion in annualized revenue for the ChatGPT maker, based on the partnership’s performance at that time, the people said.

The figures, which have not been previously reported, indicate the financial loss OpenAI is willing to take on to avoid doing business with Musk. OpenAI declined to comment. Representatives for SpaceX and Cursor did not immediately respond to WIRED's request for comment.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Is Completely Changing How You Steal Cars
highlights.summary: Carjacking in Grand Theft Auto games has been, as the title denotes, a staple of the series. Up until now, it's largely been the same. While there have been more details and animations added over the years, the premise has remained that you'll walk up to a car, press Y or Triangle, throw the driver…
body: There are two ways to steal a car: taking one that's stationary, or taking one that someone's driving around in. However, there are more details that make GTA 6 feel more like true simulation gameplay now.

As we saw in the GTA 6 extended look gameplay, when Jason approached a car, he had multiple options to choose from. The first option is a slim jim--a classic tool used to break into older vehicles. It slides down the window frame to adjust the lock, and in GTA 6, it seems like this is done via a lockpicking minigame. However, based on what we've heard so far, that won't work for every car. Depending on the year and model of the vehicle, you might not be able to use a slim jim.

However, newer and more expensive cars might not work with this method. On top of that, there are trackers, meaning that the police can track your location when you steal a car. This changes the whole carjacking aspect of Grand Theft Auto. Normally, if you'd steal a car, you might catch some heat; maybe a nearby police officer sees you and follows you, but it's pretty easy to get away cleanly. This time, that isn't the case.

highlights.title: Your home organization can actually look stylish. These 27 designer-approved solutions are proof
highlights.summary: If you feel like you’re drowning in stuff and can’t find anything you need, there’s a box (or basket) for that. 11 products our writers rely on to organize and declutter. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Look around your house and be honest: are you drowning in stuff? I know I am. Between a toddler, one on the way, two cats and a personal inability to throw out junk “just in case”, it’s rare I see the actual surface of my floor or countertops.

Without a home organization system that works for you, the sheer amount of objects you have accumulated throughout the years can quickly overrun your home. Many of us tend to put away stuff “for now”, only for our closets and cabinets to fill up, preventing us from seeing what we own. “If you can’t find something, it can feel easier to order another one than to spend 20 minutes searching,” Amy Berryhill, a professional organizer and owner of Spiffy Chicks, said.

The best way to make space for everything you need is to make intentional – and stylish! – choices about how you organize your home. “We like to think about organization as an extension of the design process, finding ways to give everyday items a designated home without sacrificing beauty,” said Audrey Scheck, an interior designer and founder of Audrey Scheck Design.

highlights.title: 150 research primates got diarrhea, flooding lab with priceless vaccine data
highlights.summary: Having more than 150 non-human primates at a research center fall ill with diarrhea in a stomach-churning outbreak that flowed for over two years doesn't sound much like good fortune.
body: In a study published in the latest issue of Science Translational Medicine, scientist sifted through the dump of immunological data from the infections, logging new ways to train immune cells to defeat the bacteria behind the outbreak, a type of Shigella. Researchers were able to pluck out specific bits of the bacteria that the immune system could most effectively attack, linking specific target molecules to specific types of germ-busting immune responses. The researchers even precisely homed in on some of the tiny notches within those craggy target molecules where the most potent antibodies attached.

In all, the study "revealed unexpected features of the anti-Shigella antibody response in naturally infected [non-human primates] and represents a step toward the rational design of Shigella vaccine candidates," the authors write.

highlights.title: Nvidia launches free tool that links idle computers into a personal AI data center
highlights.summary: Nvidia is announcing its new Personal AI Router (PAIR), a free tool that syncs up your home computers for tackling local AI inference tasks with tools like Ollama and LM Studio. Let's get the obvious thing out of the way, despite what its name might imply: PAIR is not a hardware router.
body: PAIR is designed to get your desktop and laptop working together on local AI tasks when not in use.

The key thing here is that PAIR uses your in-home systems when they’re idle to avoid interfering with other tasks. And this disaggregated system of computers can work in parallel to chew through lots of processing requests — which should be helpful for an agentic workflow that breaks complex tasks into smaller jobs. This should prevent large bottlenecks on a single GPU, and Nvidia says PAIR can adapt as devices join or leave the network — including if a user does something like start playing a game on their desktop PC.

highlights.title: Confused about which VPN is right, US senator asks the NSA for guidance
highlights.summary: A prominent US senator is asking the National Security Agency to provide guidance to the general public on best practices for using virtual private networks to secure their communications from spying by foreign adversaries.
body: VPNs funnel all of a user’s Internet traffic through an encrypted connection to a remote server. The design provides strong assurances that no one between the user and the server can read the encrypted contents. VPNs also allow users to hide their IP addresses from the destination servers they communicate with. While US agencies have previously recommended use of VPNs, none have given recommendations on which ones provide adequate protection.

There are a host of limitations that can undo many of the protections users may think their VPN provides them. For instance, the encrypted tunnel often terminates once a single server decrypts the traffic and sends it on to its final destination. That means the decrypted traffic or the sending and destination IP addresses may be available for snooping by rogue employees or attackers who hack the server. VPNs also don’t encrypt certain types of metadata, such as time stamps, allowing nation-states to build profiles that can be useful in intelligence gathering.

You can ask Gmail Live follow-up questions without starting a new conversation, and interrupt it mid-sentence if you need to pivot to something else.

highlights.title: Rust's New Force Wipe Update Includes Major Game Changes
highlights.summary: It's the first Thursday of September, which means it's the best day of the month for Rust players — force wipe. This force wipe update has been titled "Breach and Clear," as it's all about breaking obstacles and destroying lootable structures.
body: Every month, hundreds of players become prim-locked for the first few days of the wipe, as clans take over monuments and grab all available blueprints. They then have to wait for these clans to sell blueprints in their shops to finally get a Tier 2 workbench and start crafting proper weapons. To slow down their progression, Facepunch has added monument blockers to red keycard puzzle rooms. While some are weaker and can be broken with a melee weapon, others require several jackhammers to destroy. The blockers' upkeep lasts 24 hours, after which they begin to decay. This won't significantly impede progression, but it's bound to make the first day or so a bit more interesting.

The Power Trip update that went live in August made it so players had to power up the Power Plant in order to bring electricity to the entire island. To make this feature even more important, electricity across the island is now required for Outpost drones to pick up items from players' shops.

highlights.title: Gloria Steinem’s Farewell Interview to Stream on Netflix
highlights.summary: Feminist icon Gloria Steinem is the third subject to now appear on Netflix’s “Famous Last Words,” the series that banks interviews with notable figures meant to be shared only after their death. Steinem died Wednesday at her home in New York City. She was 92.
body: Per Netflix, the interview with Steinem touches on her role “as a lifelong traveler on the road to justice. While the world often recognizes her as a face of modern feminism, this interview delves into her deep-seated interests in the shared origins of sex and race caste systems, the cultures of Indigenous peoples, and the vital necessity of organizing across boundaries for equality. Steinem also takes advantage of the Famous Last Words format to speak freely about her loves, her family, the complicated personal politics within the feminist movement and her regrets.”

Steinem helped launch Ms. magazine, which was at the forefront of the movement to help organize and promote the voices and concerns of women in society. She also helped establish the Women’s Action Alliance, and wrote books including her 2015 memoir, “My Life on the Road.”
Steinem was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Obama in 2013.

highlights.title: Gloria Steinem obituary
highlights.summary: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists. Gloria Steinem, who has died aged 92, was a writer, community organiser, political campaigner and a charismatic feminist activist who called herself “an entrepreneur of social change”.
body: Steinem, unlike some of her contemporaries, never recanted or modified her many causes, which included civil rights, violence against women, and the struggle for equality. She continued to argue that every economics course ought to start not with production but with reproduction, and an understanding of the patriarchal instinct to restrict a woman’s right to contraception and abortion.

She was one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken critics throughout his rise to power. She labelled him “harasser in chief”, a man whose rhetoric and conduct ran counter to the values she had dedicated her life to advocating.

In 1963, when Betty Friedan published The Feminine Mystique – describing the frustration of affluent, well-educated, middle-class white women trapped in domesticity – Steinem was “a girl reporter” living in New York, working on The Beach Book, a compendium of extracts from literature about beaches and tips on what to do in the sun. A rising media star who was later described, to her annoyance, as “the world’s most beautiful byline”, she had already begun to make connections: she asked the economist JK Galbraith to write the foreword, and he agreed.

highlights.title: Supreme Court urged to let states regulate sports bets on prediction markets
highlights.summary: New Jersey yesterday asked the Supreme Court to rule on whether states can regulate sports betting on prediction markets such as Kalshi. “Companies like Kalshi claim to offer legal sports betting in all 50 states, but they refuse to follow the gambling laws of any state," New Jersey Attorney…
body: In April, the US Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit ruled that New Jersey cannot regulate sports bets on prediction markets. The court determined that sports-related event contracts meet the legal definition of “swaps,” giving the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) exclusive jurisdiction.

New Jersey’s petition to the Supreme Court said, “The issue is one of tremendous practical and legal consequence: Kalshi seeks to federalize the multi-billion-dollar sports betting industry at the expense of every state sports gaming law. And the decision [by the 3rd Circuit] is badly mistaken.”

New Jersey’s petition to the Supreme Court came about a week after the 9th Circuit appeals court ruled that Nevada can stop Kalshi from allowing sports bets. Unlike the 3rd Circuit, the 9th Circuit judges determined that sports betting labeled as swaps is just gambling with a different name.

The split between circuits “has tremendous importance, as it will determine whether a multi-billion-dollar gaming industry can suddenly operate free from state sports-gaming laws,” New Jersey’s petition said.

highlights.title: ChatGPT, Grok, and Claude all went down at the same time
highlights.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT, xAI's Grok, and Anthropic's Claude all began experiencing issues around the same time on Thursday. At about 11AM ET, ChatGPT started returning error messages for users trying to use the chatbot, with its status page saying there are currently "elevated errors across ChatGPT and…
body: OpenAI’s ChatGPT, xAI’s Grok, and Anthropic’s Claude are back online after they all began experiencing issues around the same time on Thursday. At about 11AM ET, ChatGPT started returning error messages for users trying to use the chatbot, with its status page saying there were “elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex.”

In addition to preventing users from having conversations with ChatGPT, the outage affected logins, file uploads, voice mode, search, deep research, image generation, and more. The incident occurred while OpenAI teased the launch of Astra, its new AI model.

Meanwhile, Anthropic’s Claude chatbot, Claude Code, and the Claude API went down around the same time, with technical staff member CJ Avilla saying an “infrastructure issue” caused a partial outage across its services. Anthropic resolved the problem at around 12:15PM ET.

Grok similarly began experiencing an outage across Android, iOS, and web at 9:30AM ET. Upon trying to prompt the chatbot on X, it returned a message saying: “This model is overloaded right now. Please try again shortly or pick a different model.” xAI has since fixed the issue, which the company linked to an outage at its Memphis data center.

highlights.title: Blizzard Might Be Teasing A New StarCraft Game
highlights.summary: There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website. While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly.
body: That would make sense. A report earlier this year said that Blizzard had partnered with Korean gaming giant Nexon to develop a new StarCraft shooter. Blizzard declined to comment on the matter at the time, and the partnership remains unconfirmed, but a report yesterday from South Korean newspaper Chosun ( via Wccftech ) reaffirms that Nexon is seeking a license to develop a new StarCraft game.

Meanwhile, Blizzard may have been working on its own new StarCraft game, as per a 2024 job posting for an "upcoming open-world shooter." Reports from that time suggested the title was in development at Blizzard, led by former Far Cry executive producer Dan Hay, who joined the company in 2022.

Another point of evidence is that BlizzCon returns on September 12 after a three-year hiatus, and Blizzard will undoubtedly want to make a splash there with big news beyond its ongoing franchises. There's also a conspicuous hour-long gap on BlizzCon's day-one mainstage programming, while all other panels only have 15 minutes of downtime between them. Sure seems like the place for something that gets announced during the opening ceremonies.

highlights.title: My dad died suddenly with no will. Am I morally obliged to share his estate with my estranged half-sibling? | Leading questions
highlights.summary: It’s kind of you to wonder if you should change the way things were left, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But it’s possible his preference is already clear. My dad died suddenly earlier this year, with no will, and I am unsure as to how I should distribute the estate.
body: My dad was a very ethical person. While his death was unexpected, he had a sense it was coming. Around six months before he died, he arranged for the disposal of many personal effects. The lack of a will, given his self-discipline and preferences for forward planning, is odd.

My dad has two daughters from a previous relationship, who he was not in contact with until I was in my mid-30s. Their mum had remarried after separating from our dad, and her new husband had formally adopted both her girls. My dad was delighted to resume contact with one half-sister. Another, two years younger, wanted nothing to do with him and firmly disapproved of her sister’s choice to re-establish contact.

Some 10 years ago, I started my own family, relocated to remove myself from domestic abuse, and joined the league of parents of children with additional needs. My dad mentioned that he had a little money put aside that could go towards legal costs, should courts ever become involved in arrangements for my son.

highlights.title: VMware migration reduces Tottenham Hotspur's licensing fees by 85 percent
highlights.summary: Tottenham Hotspur, a professional soccer team that’s part of the Premier League, has saved over 85 percent in licensing fees by replacing its stadium's VMware instance with Hewlett-Packard Enterprise’s (HPE’s) Morpheus VM Essentials (VME) virtualization software.
body: Tottenham hasn’t disclosed which VMware products it used or how much it previously paid the Broadcom firm.

The soccer organization confirmed this week to The Register that it has moved its stadium’s server, storage, and networking infrastructure to HPE solutions delivered through HPE’s hybrid cloud management platform, GreenLake. That is all “underpinned by” VME and HPE’s OpsRamp software for hybrid and multi-cloud environments, Rob Pickering, Tottenham’s CTO, told the publication, with HPE in charge of the hybrid cloud-managed service.

Tottenham is almost done with a broader redesign of its stadium’s data center and network infrastructure, The Register reported. The stadium has a data center with six aisles that uses HPE’s ProLiant Compute Gen12 server hardware and Alletra Storage MP. In an announcement this week, HPE noted that Tottenham is using “solutions including HPE Morpheus software and HPE OpsRamp software… to manage a complex, multi-site environment more efficiently while modernizing virtualization platforms and reducing operational overhead.”
“We’re at the right time of our replacement cycles to be looking at those decision points,” Pickering told SDxCentral this week.

highlights.title: Daybreak for Frontline Defenders: $1B to protect essential services
highlights.summary: OpenAI introduces Daybreak for Frontline Defenders. A $1 billion commitment expands access to frontier cyber AI, training, and support for essential services.
body: OpenAI is committing $1 billion in subsidized Daybreak access, training, technical support, and partnerships to help frontline defenders protect essential services.

Every day, we depend on cyber defenders to protect the systems that keep communities running: the water coming from the tap, the electricity powering homes and businesses, the local government systems that deliver public services, and the financial institutions people trust with their money. Many operate with limited staff and budgets, while defending complex and aging systems.

In the coming months, AI-enabled cyber attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated as models around the world become increasingly capable. That shift puts every organization on notice. Defenders need to act now: test systems, find weaknesses, and strengthen defenses before attackers do.

Frontier AI can help defenders move faster. We have a defender’s window: a narrowing opportunity to use AI to close security gaps before attackers seize them. Our role is to help put powerful tools in defenders’ hands so they can protect the systems, and the people, they are responsible for.

highlights.title: Magic: The Gathering Isn’t Done With Final Fantasy Just Yet
highlights.summary: Magic: The Gathering ’s most successful Universes Beyond crossover set ever, Final Fantasy, may have been released more than a year ago, but Wizards of the Coast and Square Enix apparently aren’t ready to put it to bed just yet.
body: Special day-one physical editions available through participating retailers will include a foil FF7 -themed Magic promo card depicting Cloud Strife clashing with Sephiroth. The card will be available while supplies last, according to Square Enix’s announcement.

The card itself is a reprint of Final Showdown, a versatile white instant originally printed as a mythic rare in 2024’s Outlaws of Thunder Junction. Its spree mechanic lets players pay for any combination of three effects: stripping every creature of its abilities for the turn, granting one creature indestructible, or destroying every creature on the battlefield.

That makes Final Showdown an unusually flexible board wipe. At its cheapest, it can protect a crucial creature for two mana. For six mana, it can destroy every creature at instant speed. Paying eight mana activates all three modes in sequence, removing potentially troublesome abilities before making one creature indestructible and destroying everything else. It's a fitting representation of a video game where a giant meteor looms in the sky, threatening to destroy the entire planet.

body: The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year, revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.

“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”

Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.

The Guy Ritchie show, which stars Theo James as a Duke gone bad opposite Kaya Scodelario’s gangland heiress Susie Glass, returns to…
body: “The Gentlemen’s” DNA can be traced back to Ritchie’s own appreciation for the country’s culture and history. “He’s his own version of Eddie Horniman,” explains costume designer Loulou Bontempts, who says the director takes a keen interest in the smallest costuming details, even down to fabric. “Tailoring is so important,” she says. “And the history behind British aristocracy and British quintessential country dressing. You know, there really are rules.”

Many such rules – for example, only the lord of the manor is allowed to wear a red velvet jacket at home — are strictly adhered to but unspoken, precisely to trip up outsiders, as newcomer Cico Maldini (played by Michele Morrone) finds out to his cost.

Having introduced audiences to the barmy world of the British aristocracy in Season 1, the show goes international in Season 2, as Eddie and Susie (Scodelario) expand their operations onto the Mafia’s home turf. “Italy felt like a very logical place in terms of the fame of the Mafia, but also the glamor,” says Read, who also executive produces the show. Cue plenty of salivating shots of Italian palazzos basking in the sun.

highlights.title: Should You Travel to Nepal Right Now? What Locals Want International Travelers to Know
highlights.summary: Whether you have travel planned, or are considering booking a trip, here's what experts on the ground say.
body: I arrive in Kathmandu on the last day of August, just five days after devastating flash floods —caused by a glacier and rock collapse along Nepal’s border with China—swept through the Rasuwa district. Entire villages and communities were wiped out, hundreds killed, and thousands more are still missing, including many tourists. It’s an unthinkable tragedy that has unfolded with devastating consequences across parts of Nepal and neighboring Tibet.

As I exit baggage claim at Tribhuvan International Airport, one of a tiny handful of non-Nepalis on my flight from Dubai, I see a Flood Related Information & Help Desk manned by police. Outside the airport, the streets are busy, a cacophony of honking horns and motorbikes buzzing between cars, buses, and tuk-tuks as people travel around the Nepalese capital. Here, at least on the surface, things seem normal.
points: Whether you have travel planned, or are considering booking a trip, here's what experts on the ground say.

I arrive in Kathmandu on the last day of August, just five days after devastating flash floods —caused by a glacier and rock collapse along Nepal’s border with China—swept through the Rasuwa district.
Entire villages and communities were wiped out, hundreds killed, and thousands more are still missing, including many tourists.
It’s an unthinkable tragedy that has unfolded with devastating consequences across parts of Nepal and neighboring Tibet.
